summary: Latah County twin-summit lookout: 1934 pole tower, 1935 steel tower moved in 1959 and removed in 1981; no source describes the site now.

facts.design: 40-foot round pole tower with an L-4 cab on the east summit (1934); a 74-foot steel Aermotor on the west summit (1935), moved to the east summit in 1959
facts.status_note: The steel tower was removed in 1981 and moved to a private summer cabin; no source describes what remains on the summits.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record's FFLA point (46.80434, -116.83933) agrees closely with the University of Idaho photo record for the lookout (46.805553, -116.840425). The second coordinate from Idaho Fire Lookouts in the record sits about 2.2 km further west; the FFLA point is kept.

firelookout.com says the L-4 pole tower was gone by 1959 (R.I.P. 1934-1959) and the Aermotor was moved to the east summit that year; both the 1959 move and the 1981 removal agree across the three sites.

notes_for_editor: Story is built on three history sources that agree on the 1934, 1935, 1959 and 1981 events. Nothing in the sources says what remains on the summits or whether the site is open to the public, so the story says so plainly. The record's second coordinate (from idaho_fl, about 2.2 km away) is not supported by the fetched pages; the FFLA point matches the Raney photo record. An AllTrails page describing a fire road to East Moscow Mountain summit was blocked (403) and is not cited. The 1951 Stedman item does not say what their role at the station was, so the event is recorded as staffed with the role left open.
